newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Dalai Lama urges Australian backing for Tibet.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Dalai Lama urges Australian backing for Tibet.

text.p: Tibet's exiled spiritual leader the Dalai Lama on Monday urged the Australian government to press China into negotiations over the future of the remote Himalayan region.
The 1989 Nobel Peace Prize winner told state radio he would seek help from Prime Minister John Howard's conservative government.
"The request or main point to ask him is help regarding meaningful negotiations with the Chinese government," the Dalai told Australian Broadcasting Corp.
The Dalai Lama arrived in Australia on Saturday for a two-week visit.
"Tibetan Buddhist culture at the moment is facing a threat of extinction ...Whether intentionally or unintentionally, some kind of cultural genocide is taking place in our country."
Howard has not yet decided if he will meet the Dalai Lama and is under pressure from the Chinese government to refuse a meeting.
Chinese Premier Li Peng warned Canberra last month against official contact with the Dalai Lama.
The exiled god-king met Foreign Minister Alexander Downer on Saturday for what Downer stressed was a private meeting.
Beijing, insisting the Dalai Lama is leading a pro-independence cause, routinely objects to other states dealing with him.
The Dalai Lama, exiled from Tibet since 1959, said a negotiated solution offered the best future for China and Tibetans.
"The best way to solve our problem is through negotiation and a negotiation that means genuine compromise and a spiritual reconciliation," he said.
"As soon as some positive indication comes from the Chinese government, I am ready to negotiate without any precondition, anywhere."
China has faced international criticism over its rule in Tibet since Chinese troops invaded in 1950.
